turns.prompt: Help me plan a small community repair café. We have one Saturday afternoon, a library meeting room, and six volunteers. Work out the repair stations, intake and safety approach, and a practical volunteer allocation. Use one semantic subcompletion for a focused review of intake and safety risks, read its findings, and integrate them into the overall proposal. Keep the work concise. Leave the supply budget as a clearly unresolved decision for now; do not assume it. Give me a useful overview with deeper supporting material only where it helps.

acceptedRootNodes.title: Keep six roles; opening is conditional
acceptedRootNodes.detail: Retain 2 textile repairers, 1 simple-household repairer, intake, queue/checkout and a protected safety lead. Reduce stations for breaks; verify skills, library approval and supplies before opening. Budget unresolved.

components.html:
Keep the allocation, with safeguards

For this Saturday library pilot: 2 textile repairers + 1 simple-household repairer + intake + queue/checkout + safety lead. Verify competence before assigning stations; shrink the offer if a skill is absent.

Keep the safety lead free of routine repairs, with authority to stop work. Stagger breaks by closing a station; do not leave intake or checkout uncovered. Pause new starts without safety coverage. Anyone may call a stop.

Before opening: obtain library approval for the exact activities/tools, confirm applicable insurance arrangements, emergency/access checks and available supplies. No supplies or funding are assumed; budget unresolved.

This is a conditional proposal, not an inspected venue or safety certification.

acceptedRootNodes.title: Screen twice; keep the scope narrow
acceptedRootNodes.detail: Intake rejects excluded items; repairers independently confirm competence, safe method and tools. Hand sewing needs an explicit needle/scissor exception. Any doubt or scope expansion means stop.

components.html:
Intake screens; repairer confirms

Advertise and enforce exclusions: mains electrical items/work, battery-powered items for this pilot, damaged batteries, gas, blades/power tools, heat/solvents and safety-critical equipment (for example helmets, brakes, medical or child-restraint equipment). Exclude contaminated, unstable or unmanageably heavy items.

Offer hand sewing and small non-powered fixes only. Resolve the textile tool ambiguity with the library: permit supervised needles and small sewing scissors explicitly, or offer only work possible without them. No irons, powered sewing machines or hidden glue/chemical exceptions.

Ask about fault, intended use, prior repair and concealed hazards before handling. Repairer then confirms skill, tools, materials and safe checks independently.

Stop: unknown hazard, out-of-scope work, missing competence/materials, unstable item, consent withdrawn or insufficient time to leave it secure. Refer or decline; consent cannot make unsafe work acceptable.

acceptedRootNodes.title: One item record through checkout
acceptedRootNodes.detail: Record consent, matching item ID and parts, proposed work, repairer checks, outcome and remaining faults. Owner stays; checkout verifies identity and explains limits, including do-not-use warnings.

components.html:
Screen → agree → repair → return

Intake: one item per person initially. Assign matching numbered tags to item, owner claim and record; describe condition, fault and detachable parts. Keep loose parts in a matching container. Collect only necessary personal data and set a retention period.

Consent: explain proposed work, risk of further damage, no guaranteed fix and the right to decline/stop. Owner stays; seek renewed agreement for changed work. Separate optional photo permission. Consent does not replace safeguards.

Queue: match skills, avoid unattended drop-offs and pause acceptance when the remaining time cannot cover repair, checks and checkout.

Checkout: repairer records work, checks, remaining faults and repaired/partial/unrepaired status. Host matches owner/item/parts and explains written restrictions or referrals. An attempted fix is not safety certification; label unsafe items “do not use” and arrange safe return, never a use demonstration.

acceptedRootNodes.title: Verify emergency and accessible operation
acceptedRootNodes.detail: Confirm venue emergency procedures, named roles, first-aid arrangements, accessible routes and seating, and controlled tools before opening. Pause the event if coverage or safe access fails.

components.html:
Brief and walk through before doors open

With library staff, confirm occupancy, clear exits, alarm, assembly point, emergency number, exact address and responder access. Name who alerts staff/calls for help, guides evacuation and meets responders. Identify first-aid provision, kit and AED location; do not assume the safety lead is trained.

Verify step-free entrance, usable toilets, clear mobility-aid routes, seated waiting and workable table heights. Offer spoken and written queue calls and help with forms; keep consent understandable. Agree evacuation assistance without requiring disclosure of diagnoses.

Keep needles/scissors controlled and counted, tools away from children, and carers responsible for supervision. Stop all repairs during an emergency, follow venue procedures and record incidents/near misses. Smoke or a suspect battery triggers staff/emergency procedures, not volunteer handling or charging.

acceptedNodes.title: Evidence and limits
acceptedNodes.detail: Primary repair-event guidance supports refusal, one-item queues, consent, item records, venue checks and emergency planning. Specific exclusions and staffing safeguards are recommendations for this proposal; no inspection or competence verification occurred.

components.html:
What supports this review

Repair Café house rules support refusing unsuitable repairs, no guaranteed outcome and one-item queues.

CCF repair agreement addresses damage risk, owner presence and return. Its safety briefing uses item IDs, outcome records and emergency briefings; its venue checklist includes access, toilets and emergency facilities.

HSE emergency guidance supports proportionate plans, clear roles, unobstructed exits and assisted evacuation.

These are general and UK-based sources, not local legal clearance. Protected staffing, stricter exclusions and handoffs are this review’s recommendations. No venue inspection, skill assessment, local policy check or supply inventory occurred; budget remains unresolved.

acceptedNodes.title: Protect safety coverage before throughput
acceptedNodes.detail: Keep the proposed 3 repairers + intake + queue/checkout + safety lead, conditional on verified skills and library approval. The safety lead should not routinely repair; pause new starts when safety coverage is absent. Budget remains unresolved.

components.html:
Keep six roles; protect the safety lead

The proposed three repairers, intake host, queue/checkout host and safety lead are a workable starting allocation only after skills and library permission are checked.

Make the safety lead a stop-work authority, not a routine fourth repairer. Pause new starts if that coverage is lost; reduce stations for breaks rather than leaving intake or checkout uncovered.

This is a staffing recommendation, not venue clearance. Supply budget remains unresolved. Screening, consent and emergency checks are being reviewed.

acceptedNodes.title: A small, bounded repair café
acceptedNodes.detail: Proposed: textiles and simple household repairs, with three repairers, one intake host, one queue/checkout host and one safety floater. Intake and safety review is pending. Supply budget remains unresolved.

components.html:
Start with low-risk repairs

Proposed stations: textiles and simple non-powered household items. Three repairers leave three volunteers for intake, queue/checkout and safety support.

Skills and library rules still need checking. A focused intake and safety review will test this setup before the proposal is finalized.

Supply budget: unresolved.
